core_obligations: Direct route: the assertion is an immediate consequence of the degree confinement statement cited at the start (proof line 3817)

First alternative: by Nakayama's lemma the smallest nonvanishing degree is the smallest degree in which Ext of the dualizing complex into the residue field is nonzero, which by duality is the smallest degree in which Ext of the residue field into the ring is nonzero, and that is the depth (proof lines 3822-3831)
Second alternative: by local duality the same smallest degree is the smallest degree with nonvanishing local cohomology of the ring, which is the depth (proof lines 3834-3838)
proof_roadmap: The statement follows immediately from the degree confinement lemma (sitting-in-degrees), cited in the first line.

First alternative: Nakayama makes the smallest nonvanishing degree delta equal to the smallest degree with Ext^{-delta}(omega, kappa) nonzero; duality rewrites that as Ext^delta(kappa, A) nonzero, and the depth-ext characterization gives the depth.
Second alternative: local duality rewrites delta as the smallest degree with nonzero local cohomology H^delta_m(A), which the depth lemma identifies with the depth.
difficulty_reason: The counted statement says that the depth of a Noetherian local ring with normalized dualizing complex is the smallest integer delta with H^{-delta} of the complex nonzero (author lemma at source lines 3808-3814, label lemma-depth-in-terms-dualizing-complex). The proof (source lines 3816-3839) states the immediate consequence of the degree confinement statement and then gives two independent derivations: one through Nakayama's lemma, duality and the Ext characterization of depth (proof lines 3822-3831), and one through local duality and the depth lemma (proof lines 3834-3838). The two substitution chains are the substance. H2.
